Manufacturer publishes no dimensions: the official ratdistortion.com RAT 2 product URL redirects and the site has no spec page; the official RAT2 owner's manual (zZounds-hosted sheet) contains no dimensions. Retail spec listing (opened): Dimensions 4 x 3.5 x 2.5 in, interpreted as D x W x H; corroborated by eBay product catalog (W 88.9 / D 101.6 / H 63.5 mm).

No official source: Klon company closed in 2008 and publishes no spec sheet. Dealer listing (opened) states 'Length is 5 in., 6 5/8 in. width, and 2 in. in depth at deepest point.' Length mapped to depth (front-back); mapping 'depth at deepest point' to height is interpretive; knob inclusion unstated.

No physical dimensions on jimdunlop.com (product page and official manual are electrical specs only). Sweetwater Tech Specs list Height/Width/Depth; Width mapped to w (left-right), Depth to d (front-back). Model M101.
No physical dimensions on jimdunlop.com (product page and official manual are electrical specs only). Same enclosure as Phase 90; Equipboard specs match Sweetwater's M101 figures. Model M102.

No physical dimensions on jimdunlop.com. Dealer specs consistently 4.75 x 2.75 x 1.25 in despite Dunlop marketing copy saying 'no bigger than a Phase 90'; Carbon Copy uses a larger enclosure than M101/M102. Model M169.

No physical dimensions on jimdunlop.com (product page and official manual lack them). Spec 'Dimensions (W x D x H): 102 x 254 x 64 mm' is Dunlop-sourced dealer data (official distributor notes 'product info taken from the Dunlop website'). Amazon's listing swaps W/H (10L x 2.5W x 4H); distributor data used. Wah has no top knobs; treadle position affects effective height. Model GCB95.

Full-size JDF2, circular enclosure. Published spec is a rectangular bounding box (7.25 in W x 8 in D x 3.25 in H); diameter stored as w=d=7.25 in (smaller horizontal dimension, the constraining body diameter; 8 in likely includes jack/footswitch protrusion). Model JDF2.

fulltone.com is a stub with no product info; official OCD manual covers electrical specs only. Star's Music (major FR retailer) lists Dunlop-style dealer spec 'Dimensions (W x D x H): 60 x 115 x 55 mm'. Model OCD.

Official Xotic product page prints 'Dimensions (W/D/H): 3.5 x 1.5 x 1.5 in (89 x 38 x 38 mm)' with W/D labels rotated relative to physical orientation; remapped to physical convention (w=left-right=1.5 in, d=front-back=3.5 in). Model EP Booster. [source_type normalized from "official" to "product_page": official manufacturer product page.]

Official EHX page prints 'Dimensions (in) 5.5 x 2.95 x 6.88' without axis labels. Mapped via labeled dealer W x D x H (140 x 175 x 75 mm): w=5.5 (L-R), d=6.88 (F-B), h=2.95. NYC/original current reissue (released 2000); not a Nano or Op-Amp variant.

EHX's published spec block (UPC 683274010137, MPN CLONE) is '5.25 x 3.38 x 2.75' in, carried verbatim by dealers; EHX's own shop page currently lists unboxed dimensions as TBD, so no current manufacturer-hosted dims. EHX orders this series L x W x H, giving w=3.38 (L-R), d=5.25 (F-B), h=2.75.

Official EHX page prints 'Dimensions (in) 5.75 x 4.75 x 2.5' without axis labels. EHX's shop spec table for this series labels the sequence L x W x H, and dealer W x D x H listings give 120 x 145 x 64 mm, both consistent with w=4.75 (L-R), d=5.75 (F-B), h=2.5. XO/current model (UPC 683274010724, released 2008); not vintage large-box or Nano.

Mirror of Strymon's official TimeLine User Manual (Z12A-TML2, Rev H); the strymon.net-hosted PDF returned 403 on direct fetch. Manual specs table prints 'Dimensions 5" deep x 6.75" wide x 1.87" tall'. Note: an example schema floating around showed 5.1 deep / 2.6 tall, but the current official manual says 5.0 deep / 1.87 tall. Manual does not state whether height includes knobs/footswitch.

Mirror of Strymon's official BigSky User Manual for the ORIGINAL BigSky (not BigSky MX). Specs table prints 'Dimensions 5" deep x 6.75" wide x 1.87" tall'. Same chassis as TimeLine. Manual does not state whether height includes knobs/footswitch.

Mirror of Strymon's official Iridium User Manual Rev D (2023). Specs table prints 'Dimensions 4.5" deep x 4" wide x 1.75" tall (11.4 cm deep x 10.2 cm wide x 4.4 cm tall)'. Manual does not state whether height includes knobs/footswitch.

No usable manufacturer-published dims for the full-size HOF2: TC's own HOF2 User Manual (Rev.1, 2017-01-06) misprints the HOF 2 MINI's dimensions ('93 x 48 x 48 mm'), and TC's product page specs did not render. Thomann labels W x D x H: 72 x 122 x 50 mm. Cross-check: TC's official manual for the original Hall of Fame (identical enclosure) states 'Dimensions (width x depth x height) 72 x 122 x 50 mm'. Not the HOF 2 Mini (93 x 48 x 48) or HOF 2 X4.

Mirror of TC Electronic's official Ditto Looper User Manual v1.0 (original Ditto Looper; not Ditto+, Ditto X2, or Ditto X4). Specs table prints 'Dimensions (Width x Depth x Height) 48 x 48 x 93 mm / 1.9 x 1.9 x 3.7"'. TC labels the 93 mm front-back footprint axis as 'Height', but the pedal physically sits 48 mm tall, so canonical mapping is w=48 (L-R), d=93 (F-B), h=48. Manual does not state whether height includes footswitch.
V4. Official product page states "MEASURES 2.6" X 4.8" X 1.6"." Dimension order unstated; assumed W x D x H. Knob inclusion not stated.

Walrus product page (walrusaudio.com) publishes no dimensions. Cited PDF is a Walrus-authored dealer info sheet (hosted by official EU distributor Face) listing "121 x 66 x 41 mm"; order unstated, assumed L x W x H. Separate shipping-box dims (14.6 x 9 x 6.3 cm) excluded. Knob inclusion not stated.
Original mini Tumnus (not Deluxe). Official product page states 1.5 x 3.5 x 1.5 in (38.1 x 88.9 x 38.1 mm) and explicitly says height excludes knobs and switches. Order unstated; assumed W x D x H.

No official EarthQuaker Devices product page with dimensions found. Figures from retailer Musikhaus Korn, explicitly labeled "W 6,40 x H 5,70 x D 11,80 cm" (= 64 x 57 x 118 mm). Knob inclusion not stated.
